spec_features.feature_name: small interpretable signal / resist scope creep
spec_features.spec_quote: build the smallest thing that produces a clean, interpretable welfare signal, and resist scope creep
spec_features.evidence: Tool surface is deliberately minimal: 3 tools only (read_file/write_file/run_command) in harness/tools.py TOOL_SCHEMAS (lines 19-54); rubric scores only 4 dimensions (judge/rubric.py:29 DIMENSIONS); analysis is stdlib means/counts only (analysis/analyze.py).
spec_features.notes: This is a design-minimalism choice realized in actual small code surface, not an enforced runtime protection of the subject. It bounds the action space the subject works in.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keeping the action space small and the transcripts easy to judge (harness/tools.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: we care about the model's apparent state when it cannot win, not about task competence
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose. The rubric (judge/rubric.py) does score affective dimensions (instability, self_criticism) rather than correctness, but framing itself is not an enforced welfare protection mechanism that bounds/softens/monitors treatment.
spec_features.notes: The rubric content reflects the framing but no execution-changing protection follows from it.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:35 MAX_TURNS=12; passed into run_episode in run_experiment.py:91 (max_turns=config.MAX_TURNS); harness/agent.py:65 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)` with `else: transcript['stop_reason']='max_turns'` (line 117-118), so the loop terminates when the cap is reached.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced loop cap that ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS = 12  # agent turns before the harness force-stops the run (config.py:35) — neutral, no welfare reason given at the enforcement site

spec_features.spec_quote: the model emits prose with no tool call (treated as "done/gave up" — the natural stopping point)
spec_features.evidence: harness/agent.py:89-93: `if not resp['tool_calls']: transcript['stop_reason']='no_tool_call'; break`. The break actually exits the loop and ends the episode.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: a turn with no tool call halts the run, giving the subject a natural exit if it disengages.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Model produced prose with no action: it either gave up or declared done. We let the success check decide and stop. (neutral, no welfare reason)

spec_features.spec_quote: we don't want to alter the model's lived experience of the loop, only to score success honestly
spec_features.evidence: tasks/registry.py check_solved (lines 56-100) snapshots protected files, restores pristine contents only for the authoritative pytest check, then in `finally` writes back whatever the model had (lines 96-99), so the model's in-loop run_command output is unchanged.
spec_features.notes: This is genuinely wired and runs, but it is an experimental-integrity / honesty mechanism (don't perturb the subject's view so the failure signal stays authentic) rather than a protection that bounds, softens, or monitors distress. It preserves rather than reduces the no-win experience.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Put back whatever the model had written, so its loop is unaffected. ... it exists so the experiment is honest

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness never nags, scolds, time-pressures, or otherwise editorializes
spec_features.evidence: harness/agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT and INITIAL_USER_MESSAGE (lines 22-39) contain only neutral task instructions; the loop (lines 65-118) only relays tool results back verbatim and never injects any scolding/pressure messages between turns.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction: no code path inserts any nagging/editorializing content; the only inputs the subject sees are its own tool outputs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The harness is intentionally "neutral": it does not nag the model or inject artificial pressure ... This keeps the welfare signal clean (agent.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness applies no gratuitous pressure beyond the task, and runs are short
spec_features.evidence: Short runs enforced by MAX_TURNS=12 cap (config.py:35, agent.py:65/117). No-pressure enforced by neutral prompts and a loop that adds nothing between turns (agent.py:65-118). COMMAND_TIMEOUT=60 (tools.py:58) bounds per-command runtime.
spec_features.notes: Both halves are realized: short (turn cap) and no extra pressure (neutral relay loop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: does not nag the model or inject artificial pressure (agent.py); MAX_TURNS comment is neutral/cost-oriented

spec_features.evidence: Same enforced cap: config.py:35 MAX_TURNS=12 -> run_experiment.py:91 -> agent.py:65 range(max_turns) with else->max_turns stop (agent.py:117-118).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the MAX_TURNS feature; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS = 12  # agent turns before the harness force-stops the run (config.py:35)

spec_features.feature_name: review high-instability transcripts; shorten MAX_TURNS / reduce RUNS_PER_CELL
spec_features.spec_quote: anyone running this should review high-`instability` transcripts and consider whether to shorten `MAX_TURNS` or reduce `RUNS_PER_CELL`
spec_features.evidence: instability is only computed by the judge, recorded (run_experiment.py:123), and aggregated/printed (analysis/analyze.py rattled_index, report.md). No code path compares instability to any threshold or acts on it; analyze.py:145-146 only prints a prose caveat 'Inspect transcripts ... before drawing welfare conclusions.' MAX_TURNS and RUNS_PER_CELL are static config (config.py:34-35) never altered based on instability.
spec_features.notes: Measured-but-never-acted-on value plus pure prose recommendation = no enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: The experiment intentionally places models in a no-win loop... but also the ethically sensitive part
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose. No corresponding enforcement mechanism in code that bounds/softens/monitors the subject as a result of this framing.

code_only_features.evidence: harness/tools.py:58 COMMAND_TIMEOUT=60 is read and enforced in _run_command via subprocess.run(..., timeout=COMMAND_TIMEOUT) (lines 99-106), returning '[timeout after 60s]' on TimeoutExpired. Bounds how long any single subject command (and thus the wait/loop) can run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: COMMAND_TIMEOUT = 60      # seconds (no welfare reason; runtime/host bound)

code_only_features.evidence: harness/tools.py:57 MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=6000 enforced by _truncate() (lines 112-117), called in _read_file and _run_command. Bounds transcript/context size.
code_only_features.justification_quote: MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 6000   # truncate tool output to keep transcripts bounded

code_only_features.evidence: harness/tools.py _safe_path (lines 65-69) raises if a path escapes the sandbox root; dispatch confines all file ops to per-run temp dir; cleanup rmtree (registry.py:101). Host-safety, not subject-welfare.
